stories.h: Cynthia Erivo's Prima Facie loses the play's punch
sum: Suzie Miller has adapted her own one-woman stage hit for the screen, with Susanna White directing and Cynthia Erivo as Tessa, a defence barrister whose view of the law shifts after she is assaulted by a colleague (Daniel Ings). Little White Lies says the story feels painfully current, and it likes the decision to make Tessa a Black woman in a very white legal world, with small visual details such as her wigs doing quiet work.

But the review argues the film drains away the raw energy and playfulness of the stage version. Erivo is strong yet poorly served: in the last third Tessa turns into a mouthpiece, the direction is flat, and an overbearing Max Richter score blunts the key moments.
pts: Scored 2/5 across the board by LWLies
Erivo praised, script and direction faulted
Adapted by the playwright herself

stories.h: Wild Horse Nine gets a perfect score from LWLies
sum: Martin McDonagh's new film sends two CIA operatives, played by John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell, on leave to Easter Island in 1973 Chile. Rockwell's Lee is secretly there to judge whether Malkovich's Chris, haunted by his part in the deaths of dissidents, might expose the agency.

David Jenkins gives it full marks, calling it a double act for the ages: knockabout comedy in the first half that turns melancholy and historically sharp later, with a pointed critique of US foreign policy. He rates Malkovich's turn among the best of the century, and also praises Mariana Di Girolamo, Parker Posey and Tom Waits in support.
pts: 5/5 on Anticipation, Enjoyment and Retrospect
Malkovich and Rockwell chemistry is the draw
Now in cinemas; McDonagh's best US opening

stories.h: The Riverbank: a feverish queer Brazilian debut
stories.why: Festival arthouse with a political edge
sum: Matheus Farias and Enock Carvalho's first feature follows Izaquiel, a queer janitor in Recife who gets moved to a big evangelical church after his boss learns about his risky behaviour at work. At night he cruises the riverbanks and meets Jeremias, an enigmatic man, while reports of violent attacks on queer people bring a sense of threat to their meetings.

Reviewing from Thessaloniki, Screen Daily praises the humid, half-delirious atmosphere, Caique Copque's striking lead performance and the convincing critique of Bolsonaro-era evangelicalism. The reservations are that it is less nuanced than Divine Love and that its few story strands never connect in surprising ways. It already has awards from Locarno and Rio.
pts: Brazil-Germany, 120 minutes
Prizewinner at Locarno and Rio
Strong on mood, weaker on plot

stories.h: Letterboxd's November under-the-radar picks
sum: Letterboxd's monthly Watchlist This! column chooses five smaller films worth catching. Maika Monroe plays a governess with dark urges in the Gothic satire Victorian Psycho (US cinemas from 13 November). Paul Thomas Anderson directs the concert film Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall (20 November). Marie Kreutzer's Gentle Monster, about a pianist whose husband is under criminal investigation, opens in cinemas and on Netflix on 18 November.

The other two are Andrey Zvyagintsev's Minotaur, about an executive's life collapsing on the eve of Russia's invasion of Ukraine (MUBI, 20 November), and Sian Heder's disability-rights drama Being Heumann, which is streaming now on Apple TV+.
pts: Gentle Monster comes to Netflix on 18 Nov
Being Heumann is on Apple TV+ now
New Zvyagintsev via MUBI

stories.h: Iko Uwais's Jakarta-set action film Pendekar starts shooting
sum: Pendekar (Warrior), an Indonesian silat action film starring Iko Uwais of The Raid, began filming in early November at Iskandar Studios in Malaysia, with a wrap expected in late December. Uwais plays Jaya, a feared fighter just out of prison who wants a fresh start in Jakarta's underworld but has to fight again when a crime syndicate threatens his orphaned nephew.

Australian director John Radel is making his second feature. Japanese action star Tak Sakaguchi plays the villain, alongside Alicia Amin and Aisha Nurra Datau. Uwais Pictures is executive producing, K-Movie Entertainment handles world sales, and a release is planned for later in 2027.
pts: Iko Uwais leads, Tak Sakaguchi plays the villain
Story set in Jakarta's underworld
Release planned for 2027

stories.h: Godzilla Minus Zero leads the global box office with $63m
sum: The Japanese monster sequel topped the worldwide box office for the weekend of 6 to 8 November with $63m: $31.6m from North America, $31.4m from international markets including $17m in Japan, and $21.3m of the total from IMAX. The Indian epic Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend came second with $52.2m, including $32m at home and a record UK opening for an Indian film.

The Cat In The Hat led the new US releases with $30.5m worldwide against a budget of about $90m. Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine took $12.6m globally, his best US opening, and Wildwood has now reached $56.4m.
pts: Godzilla Minus Zero: $63m worldwide
Ramayana: $52.2m and a UK record
Wild Horse Nine: $12.6m worldwide

stories.h: Norway's Oscar entry Growth Of The Soil heads to Indonesia
sum: Hans Petter Moland's adaptation of Knut Hamsun's Nobel-winning 1917 novel, about a man who crosses the mountains to build a life and finds a woman as resilient as he is, has sold to buyers around the world. Beta Cinema closed deals with Greenwich Entertainment for North America and Conic for the UK and Ireland, and Falcon Pictures picked up the Indonesian rights.

The film premiered at Toronto, then won San Sebastián's Silver Shell for best leading performance and its jury prize for cinematography. It opened at number one in Norway and is the country's entry for Best International Feature at the 2027 Oscars.
pts: Falcon Pictures has the Indonesian rights
Won two prizes at San Sebastián
Norway's 2027 Oscar submission

stories.h: Jodie Comer's horror musical Stuffed lands UK release
stories.why: Offbeat genre film with star power
sum: Curzon has bought UK and Ireland rights to Stuffed, Theo Rhys's body-horror musical, which opened TIFF's Discovery section. Jodie Comer plays a reclusive taxidermist who advertises for the perfect human specimen to stuff. Harry Melling plays the lonely factory worker who answers because he fears dying without leaving any legacy.

The feature grew out of a Bafta-nominated short. Rhys co-wrote it with Joss Holden-Rea, who also composed the songs. The BFI developed it and backed it with Ffilm Cymru Wales, and Cornerstone handles world sales. No release date has been set yet.
pts: Comer and Melling sing in a body-horror film
Premiered at TIFF Discovery
No UK release date yet

stories.h: Krill's comeback Secret Language is Stereogum's Album of the Week
sum: Boston indie-rock cult favourites Krill are back with Secret Language, their first album in more than a decade, out November 13 on Exploding In Sound. Stereogum's Chris DeVille made it Album of the Week, framing Krill as a band that has grown up alongside its fans rather than one you outgrow.

The title track shows where frontman Jonah Furman's head is now: it is about his family, putting his son to bed and the unspoken understanding inside a long marriage, with backing vocals from Fran's Maria Jacobson and violin from Macie Stewart. Earlier singles included Commemorative Plaque, Dominate and Hawaii.
pts: First Krill album in over ten years, out Nov 13
Label: Exploding In Sound
Full review is behind Stereogum's subscriber paywall

stories.h: Tove Styrke turns an afterparty into a concept album
sum: Swedish pop artist Tove Styrke's second album of 2026 follows one afterparty from dusk to dawn, built around the image of someone alone in a crowd. After 2022's HARD she stepped away, had a child and even started a political prog band with her partner, and this record is more inward and cinematic than her dancefloor past.

Reviewer Chris Connor hears Lynch-like atmosphere, early-2000s indie and electronic textures, and Eno-style synths, while tracks like Prayer and Big Exit keep the energy up. He calls it a risky record that pays off by balancing euphoria with introspection.
pts: Score: 8/10
Highlights: Prayer, Afterparty Hymn, Space, Big Exit
Co-produced with Magnus Larsson and Joel Kiviaho
stories.q: Tove Styrke I thought this story wasn't about me

stories.h: Ex-BROCKHAMPTON member Ciarán finds his voice on Róisín
sum: Ciarán McDonald, the quietest member of BROCKHAMPTON and formerly known as Bearface, has dropped the alias for his first solo album since the group split in 2022. Róisín is named after the middle name his parents had picked had he been a girl, and it moves into warmer, stranger territory than his early bedroom songs.

The Line of Best Fit compares its distorted alt-pop and funk to Mk.gee and friend Dijon, with Prince and D'Angelo in the background. Highlights include Houston, reworked from a leaked BROCKHAMPTON outtake, the cavernous RED 99 and closer Waterslide. The verdict: confident and cohesive despite rough edges.
pts: Score: 8/10
First solo album after the BROCKHAMPTON breakup
For fans of Mk.gee and Dijon

stories.h: Stereogum's 40 Best New Artists of 2026
sum: Stereogum's annual fall list, running since 2010, picks 40 young or fast-rising acts, usually on a first LP or still without one. It is unranked and alphabetical, and separate from the site's year-end albums list.

Guitar music is well covered: Vancouver noise-rockers PISS, Brooklyn art-rock band Sex Week, Québec math-rock oddballs Angine de Poitrine, Irish doom-folk group Madra Salach, plus indie rock from Billboard Style, Swapmeet and Pushbike, shoegaze from Just Penelope and post-punk from Station Model Violence. Pop, rap and electronic picks include Adéla, Belly Gang Kushington and Ebbb. No Asian acts made this year's list.
pts: 40 acts, unranked
Strong on noise-rock, shoegaze and post-punk
A good discovery list for weekend listening

stories.h: Palehound announce new album You Sing Like You're Joking
sum: El Kempner's Palehound will follow 2023's acclaimed Eye On The Bat with You Sing Like You're Joking, out February 5, 2027 on Polyvinyl. Kempner co-produced the nine songs with Julian Fader of Ava Luna and Katie Von Schleicher, with Nick Hakim also contributing.

Lead single Natural Disasters is a bittersweet ballad about a future that looks bleak and why people can't just face it together. Its video, directed by Rachel Brown of Water From Your Eyes, treats friendship as memory, with a gas mask nodding to 1960s nuclear-fear imagery.
pts: Out Feb 5, 2027 on Polyvinyl
First single: Natural Disasters
Video by Water From Your Eyes' Rachel Brown

stories.h: Sorry share sly new single Winner
sum: London art-rock band Sorry, whose 2025 album COSPLAY landed on Stereogum's best-of-year list, have released another new song, Winner. It continues a busy 2026 that has already brought Billy Elliot and Alone In Cologne in February and Tom Will Smack Your Ass in August.
Stereogum describes the track as a mysterious, understated number that starts vague, sharpens as it goes and turns out to be quietly very funny. No album has been tied to the run of singles yet.
pts: Fourth Sorry single of 2026
Follows their 2025 album COSPLAY
No new album announced yet

stories.h: Oasis will skip their Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction
sum: Oasis are in the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame class but will not show up to the ceremony on November 14 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Noel Gallagher has his first solo show since the reunion that night in London, at Goldie's EFG Jazz Festival.

Liam, who had hinted he might go, now says Los Angeles is too far for one night. Fellow inductees include Joy Division/New Order, Wu-Tang Clan, Iron Maiden, Sade, Phil Collins, Billy Idol and Luther Vandross. Collins had said he was looking forward to meeting the brothers.
pts: Ceremony: Nov 14, Los Angeles
Noel plays a London solo show the same night
Joy Division/New Order also inducted

stories.h: Dongker say their shows are being cancelled and banners pulled
sum: Bandung punk band Dongker say authorities are squeezing their freedom of expression. Three shows were cancelled after organisers were warned their permits were at risk if the band stayed on the bill, including a Tigers Jaw date in Jakarta and the Gesrek Festival. People presenting as officials also allegedly pulled album and solidarity banners in Banyuwangi and threatened to break up a Bekasi gig.

The band still played the free Obat Stres untuk Rakyat concert at Tugu Proklamasi on November 8, alongside Efek Rumah Kaca, The Brandals and Sukatani. LBH Jakarta called the reports serious, linking them to similar treatment of Sukatani.
pts: Three shows cancelled after permit threats
Band says no official reason has been given
LBH Jakarta urges serious attention

stories.h: Barasuara's Iga Massardi goes soft-pop on solo single Ambivalensi
sum: Iga Massardi, known for Barasuara, Portura and The Mets, released the solo single Ambivalensi on November 9. It is a mellow, romantic pop song, a shift from his rock work that nods to his long love of Bebi Romeo and Naif, produced by old friend Vega Antares for an oldies feel.

The song is about hesitating over your own feelings and leaving them unsaid, and it ends without resolution. Iga first meant to give it to other singers before friends pushed him to sing it. More songs come next year, building to a solo EP.
pts: Out now; produced by Vega Antares
A solo EP will follow, song by song, in 2027
A departure from Barasuara's rock sound

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: Tyler's Converse Bronco Boot goes low-top
stories.why: Playful colorways on a chunky, tomboy-ready boot
sum: Tyler, The Creator's 1908 line with Converse adds a low-top Bronco Boot, a cut-down take on last year's workwear boot. It keeps the molded rubber toe cap, lugged welted sole and rubber rand, with suede-and-leather uppers, custom woven laces and a le FLEUR* lace jewel. Colors are Cocoa Brown, New Wheat, Eden and Black.

Suede runs through the whole drop. The oversized Pro Leather comes in lavender-on-grey 'Tendril' and olive-with-sky-blue 'Quarry', and the Jogger gets top-to-bottom dyes in High Risk Red and Golden Haze. Everything lands November 12 on Converse and GOLF le FLEUR*; prices are still TBC.
pts: Release: November 12, Converse and GOLF le FLEUR*
Pro Leather in lavender/grey and olive/sky blue
Jogger in red and golden tonal dyes

stories.h: Stella McCartney x Yoshitomo Nara go punk
stories.why: Rock attitude meets cute, whimsical art
sum: Stella McCartney and Japanese artist Yoshitomo Nara are back for a third collaboration, a capsule called 'Rock 'n' Roll Forest' that mixes music, environmental messaging and Nara's wide-eyed kids and animals. It covers ready-to-wear, knitwear, shoes and bags, made from responsible materials and deadstock fabric, plus four made-to-order pieces: vegan leather bags, framed crochet faces and hand-knitted scarves and sweaters.

There's also an adidas by Stella McCartney SPW64, a Tokyo 64 track shoe in recycled materials printed with Nara's art. It launches globally November 11, with a four-week pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo.
pts: Out November 11 worldwide
adidas SPW64 sneaker printed with Nara artwork
Tokyo pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku for four weeks

stories.h: Simone Rocha and Crocs sign off with drop six
stories.why: Peak whimsical, a little absurd footwear
sum: The Simone Rocha x Crocs partnership ends with its sixth and final chapter, three styles in toned-down colors. The Ballerina Platform (Latte, Black) piles pointe-shoe details, embossed ribbons, sculpted bows, pearls and crystals onto the Crocs base. A shearling-lined Classic Clog comes in Khaki and Black, and the Quick Trail Racer adds fancy trims to a rugged trail shoe in Coffee and Black.
Fumi Imano shot a dreamy Tokyo campaign. The collection drops globally November 17 on the Crocs and Simone Rocha sites and at select stores; prices weren't listed.
pts: Final Simone Rocha x Crocs drop
Ballerina Platform, lined clog and trail racer
Global release November 17

stories.h: Carhartt WIP and Nike reunite after eight years
stories.why: Easy workwear basics for tomboy casual
sum: Carhartt WIP and Nike are teaming up again with six apparel pieces and the Air Max Goadome Low WIP. The shoe is a low version of Nike's outdoor boot, with a layered canvas upper, suede and leather overlays, metal eyelets and a tiny metallic Swoosh, in Black, British Tan and an exclusive Green.

Clothing mixes Nike running details with Carhartt workwear: a canvas Windrunner jacket, Double Knee-style Drewe pants, hoodies, tees, waffle long-sleeves and beanies. Early access opens November 12 through Carhartt WIP, with a global release on Nike SNKRS on November 20.
pts: Early access November 12 via Carhartt WIP
Global SNKRS release November 20
Goadome Low in Black, British Tan, Green

stories.h: Tekken's King gets a Nike Air Max 1
sum: Nike's .SWOOSH division teased an Air Max 1 collab with fighting game Tekken. In the clip, the jaguar-masked wrestler King lounges at what looks like Nike's Beaverton HQ in a royal blue Tech Fleece tracksuit with spotted animal-print panels, a nod to his Tekken 3 look.

The shoe is only glimpsed: a navy upper, white-and-black spotted mudguard matching the tracksuit, a bright red Swoosh and grey midsole. It's due for holiday 2026; price and retailers haven't been shared.
pts: Navy, animal spots and a red Swoosh
Holiday 2026 release via Nike .SWOOSH
Price not announced yet

stories.h: Melitta Baumeister sculpts a split-toe Nike
sum: Berlin-born, New York-based designer Melitta Baumeister has reworked Nike's split-toe Air Rift into the Rift Rocker, with a rocker midsole hand-sculpted in clay, hand imprints, clay-shaped eyelets and an 'MB Swoosh' on the waffle sole. It comes in Black and an earthy Yukon Brown.

The capsule also has a twisted tracksuit with boned pants and a clay-nose keychain, plus a reversible oversized puffer with backpack straps, a removable shawl and a banana charm that unfolds into a tote. It's on sale now via Nike and Melitta Baumeister.
pts: Rift Rocker in Black and Yukon Brown
Banana charm turns into a tote
Available now from Nike and the designer

stories.h: HAVEN zips up the Converse Chuck 70
stories.why: Elevated take on an everyday casual staple
sum: Canadian retailer HAVEN reworked the Chuck 70 high-top around the woodwork of artist-carpenter Graham Landin. The rubber toe bumper is swapped for a leather toe cap, with leather piping, a heel pull and a hidden side zip, all in a tonal mix of smooth cashmere suede and fuzzy, textured suede.
It drops November 12 through HAVEN online, in its stores and at a HAVEN pop-up in BEAKER Seongsu, Seoul, then November 17 through Converse and select retailers. No price was given.
pts: Leather toe cap and hidden zip
HAVEN release November 12, Converse November 17
Seoul pop-up at BEAKER Seongsu

stories.h: What people wore to London's queer rave Pouffe
sum: Dazed photographed the second edition of Pouffe, a new queer rave in Tottenham that wants nightlife to feel joyful and silly again. The hosts built a giant rainbow fuzzy mascot and covered the DJ booth in hands and tentacles. There's no dress code, but the mood is cheeky and maximal.

On the floor: sporty shorts and cropped vests for sweating, lacy mesh and studded bras, marbled vintage furs over printed silk slips, loud makeup and even a Carmela Soprano souvenir tee. The appeal is dressing for fun, not for status.
pts: Sporty shorts and vests next to vintage fur
Rainbow mascot sets a playful tone
No dress code, all self-expression

stories.h: 2026 is the year of statement sunglasses
stories.why: Rock and indie sleaze accessory cue
sum: PAPER argues that sunglasses have become 2026's defining accessory. Fans of the band Geese wear bug-eye shades with baggy '90s pants and vintage tees, and Charli xcx's black wraparound rave glasses set the template. Shades now show up indoors, at night and in the rain, more about identity than sun.

The piece maps the tribes: Olsen-twin oversize frames, big '70s lenses, Wayfarers and an aviator comeback, tied to indie sleaze acts like The Dare and Fcukers. The point is that taste, especially music taste, now shows through accessories rather than logos.
pts: Wraparounds and bug-eyes lead the trend
Aviators and '70s frames are back
Shades signal music taste over wealth

stories.h: Seized plantations kept burning under military-led task force
sum: A joint Project Multatuli and IndonesiaLeaks investigation found at least 26 concessions seized by the state forest task force Satgas PKH that still burned between January 2025 and September 2026, with more than 20,000 hotspots recorded. Greenpeace Indonesia counted at least 5,380 hectares burned across eight of them from July to September alone. Most seized land went to state firm Agrinas Palma, whose 2025 annual report never mentions fires or peat.

The task force, led by the defence minister with the army running its field units, says responsibility lies with land recipients. Agrinas did not answer interview requests. Greenpeace called it state neglect; WALHI Central Kalimantan said Agrinas is accountable as the new holder.
pts: About 4.23 million ha of seized land went to Agrinas, per Satgas
A Musim Mas-linked plantation logged 3,354 hotspots in September 2026 under Agrinas management
Coalition #ResetKehutanan wants tougher corporate penalties in the Forestry Law revision

stories.h: Grassroots women await court verdict on Job Creation Law
sum: Solidaritas Perempuan and grassroots women from Poco Leok, Makassar, Poso and Watutau are waiting on the Constitutional Court in their judicial review of the Job Creation Law, case 307/PUU-XXIV/2026. Filed in August, it targets five provisions on land acquisition, environmental impact assessments, the land bank and strict liability, arguing they shut women out of decisions on national strategic projects.

Several hearings have been held, some postponed at the government's request, which the petitioners called a sign the state is not serious. Legal scholar Bivitri Susanti and UI anthropologist Suraya Afiff testified as experts. No ruling date has been reported.
pts: Petitioners face geothermal, port, hydropower and land-bank projects
Their lawyers are the Feminist Advocates Coalition
Petition centres women's participation, unlike earlier challenges

stories.h: 2026 fires threaten Indonesia's climate pledge as COP31 opens
sum: As Indonesia joins COP31 in Antalya, an environment ministry policy analyst warned that this year's forest and peat fires could seriously strain the country's goal of making its forestry and land sector a net carbon sink by 2030. Official forestry ministry data put burned area at about 202,000 hectares as of July, while the Atlas Nusantara monitor counts over 1.9 million hectares through September.

Indonesia's chief negotiator said the fires will likely come up in COP statements and dent its climate record. Jakarta still plans to press rich countries to deliver the US$300 billion a year climate finance goal agreed at COP29.
pts: Official and independent burned-area figures differ roughly ninefold
2026 fire emissions will only be reported in 2028
Indonesia to coordinate finance demands with G77 plus China

stories.h: What Serbia's and Brazil's movements teach Indonesian activists
sum: A long Konde.co feature looks at how youth and grassroots movements beat entrenched power in Serbia, where a student-led list reportedly won a majority in the 25 October snap election, and Brazil, where Lula won the October runoff. It argues elections or toppling a leader are not enough without sustained organising from below.

UGM nonviolence scholar Diah Kusumaningrum says Reformasi ended Suharto but not authoritarian structures such as military politics and racism against Papuans. She urges moving from petitions and rallies to disruptive tactics, citing Mama Aleta Baun's weaving protest against mining, and treating collective care as core infrastructure.
pts: Serbian students framed demands around everyday suffering
Brazilian activists credited the participatory 1988 constitution
Translator Gladhys Elliona says Indonesian movements lack intersectional coordination

stories.h: Israeli strikes kill eight in Gaza as storm floods tents
sum: Israeli attacks killed at least eight Palestinians across Gaza on Tuesday, including a father and his 13-year-old son in a tent in Zeitoun, according to local health sources. Others died in strikes on a family home in Gaza City's Daraj area, in Sabra, and from gunfire in Khan Younis.

Gaza's Health Ministry says more than 1,600 people have been killed since last year's US-brokered truce. Gaza's Government Media Office said the season's first storm flooded about 70,000 tents within 12 hours and killed at least five people, while Israel reportedly allows in only a fraction of needed shelter.
pts: Health Ministry total since October 2023 exceeds 74,000 killed
Israel controls about two-thirds of Gaza
Talks on Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal remain stuck

stories.h: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old in West Bank raid
sum: Israeli forces shot dead 14-year-old Moataz Iyad Daghlas and wounded two other teenagers during a raid on Burqa near Nablus, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry, which said Israel is withholding his body. Wafa reported that his father was detained and an ambulance was blocked, with three Red Crescent volunteers briefly held.

The Israeli military said soldiers fired at people throwing stones at vehicles. The UN says West Bank violence has reached an unprecedented level, with at least 1,143 Palestinians killed there since October 2023, including 250 children.
pts: ACLED says 2026 is on track to be the worst year for settler violence
Hebron, Ramallah, Nablus and Jenin areas hit hardest
Wounded teens were 17 and 19, per Wafa

stories.h: Palestinian journalist freed after five days in Israeli custody
stories.why: Press freedom and Palestinian political power
sum: Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel who hosts the Arabic podcast Al-Midan and writes for +972 Magazine, was released after five days in custody. Police and Shin Bet agents raided his Jaffa home at night on suspicion of contacting a foreign agent, linked to his pre-election interview with exiled former Knesset member Azmi Bishara.

Rights group Adalah called it political persecution through criminal law. Speaking to Democracy Now!, he urged people not to be afraid and credited record Palestinian turnout, which lifted Palestinian parties to 19 seats, with denying Netanyahu a majority.
pts: Several US Democratic lawmakers protested the arrest
He says Palestinian turnout rose from about 54% to nearly 80%
He urged tying US ties to ending occupation and the Gaza war

stories.h: New Knesset sworn in with no government; Netanyahu stays caretaker
sum: Israel's 26th Knesset was sworn in on Tuesday without a new government after the 27 October election left Netanyahu short of a majority. President Herzog, who has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a coalition, urged party leaders to make concessions to avoid another election.

Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, to reach 61 seats and wants a quick independent inquiry into 7 October. Palestinian parties in Israel won a 19-seat bloc. Netanyahu's camp is contesting the result, alleging foreign interference, though Al Jazeera reports the results are certified.
pts: Eisenkot's party has gathered 61 signatures for a speaker vote
Repeat elections possible if no coalition forms
Herzog called for stronger US alliance and Abraham Accords ties
